subject: Perfect observers in occupancy model causes model to fail

messages.author: 8a67cb9308a430d7
messages.subject: Perfect observers in occupancy model causes model to fail
parts:
We am trying to build a species based site occupancy model but our observers might be slightly different from the normal set of observers because they are either “perfect” observers (e.g. they identify the species in all sites) or they are “terrible” observers (e.g. they never identify the species in all sites). I haven’t been able to find any indications this should be a problem in either MacKenzie et al. 2006 “Occupancy Estimation and Modeling” or Kery and Royle 2016: “Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology”, BUT we get the Error message: “Hessian is singular. Try providing starting values or using fewer covariates.”.

 

We have tried removing all covariates, and we have tried with various starting values without luck. We are therefore considering whether the issue is related to the nature of our observers and the lack of variation in their observability. This was confirmed when inputting false variation in the observer behaviour led to the model succeeding.

 

Has anyone experienced similar problems and/or does anyone have any idea why we might experience these issues.

 

This is my first time on the forum, so happy to elaborate if anything is unclear or the approach is wrong.

 

Best, Jonas

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Perfect observers in occupancy model causes model to fail
parts:
Dear Jonas,

depends on what you mean by "they identify the species in all sites". If this means that the species REALLY occurs everywhere in your sampled sites, then occupancy is 100% and hence constant over sites and there is nothing to be explained by any site covariates. In that case, the only thing that varies is detection probability (p), being 100% for the good observers and some smaller percentage for the bad observers. If you are interested in estimating p for them and their relationship with the covariates, then you could simply fit a logistic regression for instance with function glm() in R.

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.author: 8a67cb9308a430d7
messages.subject: Re: Perfect observers in occupancy model causes model to fail
parts:
Dear Marc

 

Thank you very much for the reply – and sorry if I didn’t describe the problem clearly. So its not that they identify species in all sites within the total area of interest (S) – only all the sites they visit (s) which is a smaller fraction of the total number of sites in the study area. For the individual sites there will be some with no detection at all, and some where all observers surveying found the species – and everything in between.

 

Thus, for sites (rows), there will be 1s = species observed, 0s = species not observed and NAs = observer didn’t survey the site.

 

But, for the individual observer (columns) there will be two distinct types: observer 1: only 1s or NAs and observer 2: only 0s or NAs.

 

I haven’t been able to find any indication this should cause problems, but imputing variability in the columns/observers does led to the model running.

 

Best, Jonas
